subject: Human Body
title: Veins and Venous Return
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Veins and Venous Return.

hook.text: Veins carry blood back to the heart under low pressure. Unlike arteries, they need help from muscles and valves.

buildup.text: One-way valves inside veins prevent backflow. Blood can only move toward the heart, not away from it.

discovery.text: Skeletal muscles squeeze veins when you walk. This muscle pump pushes blood upward against gravity.

twist.text: Standing still for hours defeats the muscle pump. Blood pools in the legs, causing dizziness and fainting.

climax.text: Varicose veins form when valves fail. Blood pools and stretches the vein walls into visible, twisted cords.

punchline.text: Veins depend on your muscles. Keep moving and blood flows.

quiz.question: What helps push blood through veins against gravity?
options: Skeletal muscles squeezing veins with one-way valves
Smooth muscle in the vein walls
